\[

y_{\rm blur}\;=\;L\;\sin\theta_{\rm blur}
\;=\;L\,\frac{\lambda_{2}}{\pi\,d}\,
\sqrt{\frac{m\,c^{2}}{k_{B}T}}\; }
\]

**Derivation sketch**

1. In the far‑field the optical path difference between the two slits is  
   \(\Delta = d\sin\theta\).

2. Because the sodium atoms move thermally, the emitted line at wavelength  
   \(\lambda_{2}\) is Doppler–broadened. For a Maxwellian velocity distribution the
   one‑dimensional speed spread is Gaussian with standard deviation  

   \[
   \sigma_{v}= \sqrt{\frac{k_{B}T}{m}} .
   \]

   Hence the corresponding wavelength spread (standard deviation) is  

   \[
   \sigma_{\lambda}= \frac{\lambda_{2}\,\sigma_{v}}{c}
   =\lambda_{2}\sqrt{\frac{k_{B}T}{m\,c^{2}}}\; .
   \]

3. For a source with a Gaussian spectral distribution the fringe visibility
   (contrast) is  

   \[
   \gamma(\theta)=\exp\!\Big[-\Big(\frac{\pi\,d\sin\theta\,\sigma_{\lambda}}
   {\lambda_{2}^{2}}\Big)^{2}\Big].
   \]

4. The fringes are regarded as “blurred’’ when the visibility has fallen to
   \(1/e\) (the same level at which a background of intensity \(I_{\max}/e\)
   would make the pattern appear dim). Setting \(\gamma=1/e\) gives  

   \[
   \frac{\pi\,d\sin\theta_{\rm blur}\,\sigma_{\lambda}}{\lambda_{2}^{2}}=1
   \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\;
   \sin\theta_{\rm blur}
   =\frac{\lambda_{2}}{\pi d}\sqrt{\frac{m\,c^{2}}{k_{B}T}} .
   \]

5. With the screen at distance \(L\) (small‑angle approximation
   \(\tan\theta\simeq\sin\theta\)), the linear coordinate of the first blurred
   fringe is  

   \[
   y_{\rm blur}=L\sin\theta_{\rm blur}
   =\frac{L\,\lambda_{2}}{\pi d}
   \sqrt{\frac{m\,c^{2}}{k_{B}T}} .
   \]

This expression gives the position on the observation screen where, for the
first time, the interference fringes become perceptibly blurred due to the
thermal (Doppler) broadening of the filtered sodium line.  (All symbols have
their usual meanings: \(c\) – speed of light, \(k_{B}\) – Boltzmann constant.)
